items.title: fix(id): reject world_created replies with a missing or mistyped created flag (#6632)
items.body: Fixes #6632. `WorldClient::create_world` read the `world_created` reply's outcome flag with a silent default — `reply["created"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false)` — so a reply whose `created` field was missing or mistyped (host bug, version skew) read as "the world already existed": `id world create` printed `exists` and exited 0 for a world whose creation was never confirmed. ## Change (`pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs`) - Factor the reply tail into `parse_create_world_reply`, following the `parse_module_info_reply` precedent (#6633): the refusal path still surfaces the host's message (or the existing default), a well-formed reply returns `Ok(true)`/`Ok(false)` unchanged, a missing `created` errors with "host sent no created flag in world_created reply", and a present-but-non-boolean `created` errors as a malformed `world_created` reply. Fail-closed is preserved — an unreadable flag never grants or confirms anything; the fix is visibility, not leniency. - Regression test `create_world_reply_requires_created_flag` drives the factored parser: both controls, missing flag, mistyped shapes (string / number / null / array), and both refusal shapes. Oracle: the sibling strictness of `parse_module_info_reply` — a present-but-wrong-shape field is corruption, not a default. ## Verification - Laptop (worktree @ 62377a73ee): `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/id/Cargo.toml --lib create_world_reply` — `world_net::tests::create_world_reply_requires_created_flag` ok (1 passed). - Laptop: sibling parser test `info_details_rejects_malformed_active_module_hash` ok, and the existing create-world-over-iroh test `world_session::tests::tests::only_an_admin_creates_or_lists_worlds` ok (EXIT:0). - rustfmt clean on `pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs`. Filed from a fallback-mode queue shift (queue backend down, code#6619): the issue was claimed and released via `fleet-claim` markers on #6632 by `repo-worker-code-l`. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(id/world_net): refuse a malformed compiled reply instead of defaulting its fields (#6620)
items.body: Closes #6620 ## Summary `WorldClient::compile` read the host's `compiled` reply with `unwrap_or_default()` on every field — a missing or mistyped `module_hash`, `sequence`, or `diagnostics` silently became `("", 0, "")` and `Ok`, so `id world compile` printed an empty hash with exit 0 and `id world apply` counted the step applied. `compile()` now routes through a factored `parse_compile_reply` (mirroring `parse_create_world_reply`, landed for sibling #6632) that: - bails with the host's message on a non-`compiled` frame (refusal path unchanged, default "host refused to compile"); - requires `module_hash` and `diagnostics` to be present strings and `sequence` a present unsigned integer, failing with errors naming the field ("host sent no module hash in compiled reply", "host sent a malformed compiled reply: `sequence` is not an unsigned integer", …); - returns well-formed replies unchanged, including a genuine sequence `0` and empty diagnostics. Phase 1 of design #6669 (a reply is not its defaults); error wording follows the #6632 precedent in the same file. ## Evidence - New regression test `compile_reply_requires_all_fields` drives the parser with the issue's shapes: well-formed control returned unchanged; genuine `sequence: 0` + empty diagnostics control; each field missing → error naming the field; bare `{"type":"compiled"}` → error; mistyped fields (number-as-hash, string/negative sequence, number diagnostics, null hash) → error; refusal frames surface the host's message and the default refusal text. - `cargo test --lib compile_reply_requires_all_fields` (laptop, pkgs/id): passed. Full `cargo test --lib world_net` (laptop): 29 passed / 0 failed. - The defect was verified at claim on origin/main `b7d16d10`: `world_net.rs:772-776` still carried the three `unwrap_or_default()` reads while every sibling parser in the file refuses the same shapes. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way — client-side validation only, single-commit revert. **Blast Radius:** `WorldClient::compile` callers only (`id world compile`, `id world apply`'s InstallModule step). Well-formed hosts (the typed server always sends all three fields) are unaffected; only missing/garbled `compiled` replies change, from silent `("", 0, "")` success to an explicit error naming the field. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(id): pin documented skip policy for unknown marks (#1045)
items.body: Follow-up to #1045 triage (task 6632). Unknown marks are now an explicitly documented skip-by-design policy on `prosemirror_to_markdown` (text survives, unknown styling is shed), distinct from unknown nodes which keep returning `ConversionError::UnknownType`. - Doc comment on `prosemirror_to_markdown` naming the policy - Clarified skip arm in `create_marked_text` (`code` vs unknown marks) - Regression test `test_unknown_marks_are_skipped_by_design`: bare unknown mark, mixed known+unknown, code+link+unknown Tests: `cargo test --offline --features web --lib web::markdown` — 224 passed, 0 failed (stub `web/dist`, gitignored, required for rust-embed compile). Closes #1045. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Markdown conversion now preserves text when it has unrecognized formatting, while continuing to render supported formatting.
